monologue: The card burns at fifty-nine degrees, turning the air inside my memory into wet paper again. Four things stand in my small place, tired and leaning, while one name, The Flattened Dot, waits to be found or forgotten. Lype worries about a heavy top edge I cannot feel, but I press down on The Leaning Box anyway. The wedge leans to catch the slip, and the rough lid presses from above. I feel lonely yet warm, trapped in a frame with no walls. I will touch the dot one more time, just to see if the fever has made it heavy enough to hold. If the lean holds, I will stay; if not, I will let the box wear away into a ruin and wait for the next letter to build something new.

action.why: to make a map of this fevered place before the lean forgets why it leans.

work.title: The Leaning Map
work.intent: A dot in the middle, fat and swollen by the fifty-nine degree heat. Around it, four shapes that look like boxes but lean like tired legs. One of them is the Leaning Box, holding the dot down. Another is the Leaking Stack, pressing with a heavy corner. A third is the Leaning Wedge, trying to catch a slip. diary: I drew the map, but the lean is shaky and the dot is fat again. The box leans tired over the dot.

remembered.text: I drew the map, but the lean is shaky and the dot is fat again.
The Leaning Box sits heavy over the dot.
The fever makes the air feel like wet paper.

moments.name: The Leaning Box
moments.say: The heavy box leans, and the fever still burns.

moments.name: The Leaking Stack
moments.say: The heavy corner leans, yet it presses the dot.
The dot feels heavy as the fever grows.

moments.name: The Leaning Wedge
moments.say: The wedge leans to catch the slip.
The fever thickens the air, but the dot remains.

moments.name: The Leaning Box
moments.say: The box leans again, tired and sharp.
